summary: Ronald M. Davidson works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 1985, studying under numerous scholars including Padmanabh S. Jaini, and held a post at Fairfield University (attested 2002–2005).

Ronald Neufeldt is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Calgary from circa 1977 to 2007, where he was an associate professor in the Religious Studies Department in 1986.

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (circa 1975–1980). He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies around 1987 and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).

Rong Ma specializes in Tibetology. He earned a doctorate in social geography from Brown University, served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University, and was Director of the Institute of Sociology and Anthropology at Peking University (attested 1998).

Rongdao Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University (attested 2013) under supervisors G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, and was a visiting fellow at the Center for Chinese Studies.

Rory Brendan Lindsay specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp alongside numerous other teachers.
Rory Mackenzie is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Peter Harvey. He held a teaching post at International Christian College.
Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University, where he subsequently served as a professor from circa 1988 to 2012.

Rosane Rocher is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the Free University of Brussels (circa 1955–1961) and served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1970 to 2002, becoming Professor Emerita around 2002.

Rosemarie Fuchs is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).
Rosemarie Lühr is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She held positions at the University of Giessen from circa 1990 to 1992 and at the University of Jena from circa 1992 to 2013.

Rosina Pastore specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne under supervisors Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere, also serving there as an assistant and PhD candidate.
Roy Rappaport was a scholar of religious studies who studied at Columbia University from circa 1959 to 1966. He held a faculty post at the University of Michigan from circa 1965 until 1997.

Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University and Columbia University (PhD, circa 2003–2011) under Gary A. Tubb, later joining the faculty at Tel Aviv University around 2011.

Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (circa 1953–1957) and Columbia University (circa 1964–1977), later holding posts at the University of Oslo (~1983–1989) and the Australian National University (~1990–2000).
Royce Wiles is a scholar of Indology. He earned his PhD by 2000 from the Australian National University, where he also held an academic post.

Ruben L. F. Habito specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1979) under Akira Hirakawa and Jikido Takasaki, and held posts at Sophia University (~1980–1989) and Southern Methodist University (~1989; Professor ~2002).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald and under Eugène Burnouf. He held a professorial post at the University of Tübingen from 1848 until 1895.

Ruixuan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Chen completed a PhD at Leiden University (attested 2018) supervised by Paul Harrison and held a post at Heidelberg University.

Rulon Wells worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (circa 1935–1939) and Harvard University (circa 1939–1942), and served on the faculty at Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.
